passage: L1.1: "Using the same dataset for training and testing the model is a textbook example of overfitting" (Results, 'Toward a solution: A taxonomy of data leakage', PMC10499856; as returned by the fetch tool).
faulty: Ordinary least squares (intercept, 25 features) fitted on all 60 rows; skill = 1 - MAE(fitted values)/MAE(mean predictor) on the same 60 rows; holds iff >= 0.10.
fixed: 5-fold cross-validation (fold = i mod 5), OLS fitted on 48 rows predicts 12; pooled MAE against the training-fold mean predictor; skill >= 0.10.
estimand: Faulty: apparent MAE skill of a model fitted to all 60 samples. Fixed: expected out-of-sample MAE skill.
model_family: Ordinary least squares on 25 raw features with intercept (numpy lstsq). Chosen to differ from the ridge model of B2A-01: unpenalised, a moderate p/n of 0.42.
sizes_note: Source states none. 60 x 25 = 1,500 values, a small-sample regime in which the in-sample skill under no effect is about 0.24 (reserve for L1.1). Dependence on sample size or feature count: not stated.
exploited_structure: Many features relative to samples, so the fitted model reproduces the outcomes of the rows it was fitted on.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: 25 features / 60 samples is the brief's own size; set by the brief

notes: Reserve for L1.1. Guard: None if MAE of the mean predictor is zero; non-finite returns None. Differs from B2A-01 and B2A-02 in family (other), model and sample-size regime.
